**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR allows the kubelet to synchronize completed pods until their containers have been terminated.

If a pod was evicted, its `containerStatuses` were out of sync because `dispatchWork` did ignore works of the pods having completed.

@gjkim42 Thanks for this PR. I did some testing, and while the PR seems to address the original issue I noticed a couple of things,

1. It takes a significant amount of time (about 5min in my testing) for the container status to change from `running` to `terminated` **after** pod phase has changed to `Failed` due to reason `DeadlineExceeded`. I am suspecting that's because my pod yaml has `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` set to [300](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98718#issue-800125055). 
```

  - containerID: cri-o://235c3f643add7dbfc88fc3607918b652dabca435521a4e042bc27e61df6ff365
    image: docker.io/library/busybox:latest

    lastState: {}
    name: test
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    state:

  qosClass: Burstable
  reason: DeadlineExceeded

```

It looks like this partially regressed / altered very short running pod behavior (create -> <short> -> delete -> <very long cleanup>).  That's because there's a race condition between the check done here and the PLEG - it's not safe for dispatchWork to check statusManager in podAndContainersAreTerminal because statusManager is out of date at the time the PLEG entry shows up.

We need to fix the fundamental problem that these two optimizations were aimed at, but we can't do that safely without synthesizing the podCache data from PLEG.  Ultimately the syncPod loop is the one responsible for this calculation and we need to fix the problems that led to us pulling logic outside of it.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/102025#issuecomment-843622820

This may have impacted the change, but it didn't actually solve it.  We'll be opening a new issue to address the root cause.

issue_context.title: Incorrect container status when pod exceeds activeDeadlineSeconds
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When pod exceeds `activeDeadlineSeconds` we find that,

```
status:
  containerStatuses:
  - containerID: cri-o://e3c8354c818791d37fb6fee96465075344ec2116f95edb5ddb3269d7d5d5f297
    image: docker.io/library/busybox:latest
    imageID: docker.io/library/busybox@sha256:0415f56ccc05526f2af5a7ae8654baec97d4a614f24736e8eef41a4591f08019
    lastState: {}
    name: test
    ready: false
    restartCount: 0
    state:
      running:
        startedAt: "2021-02-01T12:29:17Z"
  message: Pod was active on the node longer than the specified deadline
  phase: Failed
  podIP: 10.128.2.23
  podIPs:
  - ip: 10.128.2.23
  qosClass: Burstable
  reason: DeadlineExceeded
  startTime: "2021-02-01T12:29:14Z"
  ```
The pod `phase` is correctly states `Failed` with the reason `DeadlineExceeded` but as you can see above the container state is still reported as `running` 

**What you expected to happen**:
Container state should be `Terminated` not `running` because pod has exceeded `activeDeadlineSeconds`

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
```yaml
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  metadata:
    name: test
  spec:
    activeDeadlineSeconds: 200
    terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300
    containers:
    - args:
      - "600"
      command:
      - sleep
      image: docker.io/library/busybox
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      name: test
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 10m
          memory: 10Mi
```
Create the pod described above and wait till it exceeds listed `activeDeadlineSeconds`.  Then get the container status using,
`kubectl get -o yaml pod test | grep -A1000 '^status:'` 

**Anything else we need to know?**:
